description: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The Brazil IEEPA 40% carve-out was conditioned on the witness's aluminum exemplar line 7601.10.30.00 (`entry_is_line_b`) rather than on Section 232 aluminum membership, which is the condition 9903.01.83 actually states as the exception to 9903.01.77.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 36; diff read individually, identical hunk shape. Chapter 39 (plastics) contains Section 232 aluminum/steel derivative articles in principle, so the pre-fix gate could add +40% to Brazil-origin entries the order excepts. Steel citation hunks are provenance only (0.50 rate unchanged).
triage.verifier_justification: The diff changes the gating condition of a source-stated carve-out inside `ieepa_component_rate` and `ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions` (versions[0].formula, from 2026-02-15), so encoded meaning changed, not just provenance. The module's own proof atom for that branch cites us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-219, "The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02", and the pinned release confirms 9903.01.77 imposes Brazil +40% "Except for products described in headings 9903.01.78-9903.01.83" with 9903.01.83 naming classes ("articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum; ..."), never a single HTS line. The pre-fix condition `entry_is_line_b` is the hand-built witness's per-line aluminum exemplar flag (7601.10.30.00, a chapter-76 line) with no basis anywhere in the cited text, so in a generated chapter-39 composition the carve-out could never fire and the 40% was applied to ch39 Section-232-aluminum derivative articles the source excepts — the module itself branches on `entry_is_section_232_aluminum` for its aluminum component, so such ch39 entries exist. The fix re-grounds the branch on the membership class the source states, which is untraceable_branch rather than a mis-scoped source concept (wrong_entity_or_scope is the runner-up).

triage.verifier_notes: Refutations I tested and rejected: (1) "Pure generalization / new coverage the module never claimed" — rejected, because the module already carried the carve-out and already cited the 9903.01.77 exception as a proof atom (unchanged in the diff), so it claimed the meaning it encoded wrongly; the PR's own framing ("move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs") is the mechanism, not proof that the old text was right. (2) "Behaviorally inert in ch39" — rejected, since the same file has `section_232_steel_component_rate`/`section_232_aluminum_component_rate` branches for chapter 39 and the resolved note page listing covered lines includes chapter-39 lines (3917.31.00, 3926.90.94, ...), so real ch39 entries hit the changed branch. (3) "Whole diff is provenance" — rejected for the anchor, but true for the rest: the `ch39_s232_steel_heading_rate` / `section_232_steel_component_rate` half (9903.81.87/.88 → 9903.82.02, plus the `source:` string) is citation/excerpt-only, with formula `'0.50'` and the steel formulas byte-identical, i.e. mechanical. Caveats for the reviewer: the first reader's cited heading 9903.01.83 is substantively right but the module's own atom uses the page-219 / 9903.85.02 aluminum formulation; the post-fix gate is still under-inclusive versus 9903.01.83 (which also excepts steel, wood, vehicles, semiconductors, copper) though it now matches the module's cited aluminum-only excerpt; and the same exemplar proxy survives unfixed at `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` (formula `entry_is_line_b`, cited to 9903.01.33 "articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum") in both pre and post — a residual instance of the identical defect worth flagging separately.
